## 1. Market sizing – bottom-up, US only

**Blended price:** use one recurring software price for all segments.

| Vendor | Annualized recurring price | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BinSight | $149 x 12 = **$1,788** | pricing page, 2025 |
| Kitchen Ledger | **$2,400** (excl. $1,500 one-time kit) | pricing page, 2025 |
| Scrapless | $179 x 12 = **$2,148** | pricing page, 2025; ignore $99/mo 2021 as superseded |
| Wastewise | **$2,100** ACV | data room |
| **Blended** | (1,788+2,400+2,148+2,100)/4 = $2,109 → **use $2,100** | average of current list/ACV, hardware excluded |

Kitchen Ledger Year-1 TCO is $3,900, but TAM/SAM use recurring only for comparability.

**Segment choice:**
- **TAM = Full-service restaurants + Institutional kitchens.** Operationally viable for camera+scale: prep-waste volume and space.
- **Excluded from TAM:** Limited-service 385,840 locations [385,840 = 742,000 x 52%] – franchisor-mandated inventory tools, standardized portions, "not a near-term buyer" [4]; Other bars/trucks 74,200 [742,000 x 10%] – minimal prep waste, no space.
- **SAM = Institutional 96,000 only.** 11% already penetrated [4], 70% of Wastewise base is here with lower churn. Full-service stays in TAM as long-term upside only – 3% penetrated [4] and Wastewise 14% logo churn concentrated in independent full-service [7] shows no repeatable fit yet.

| Market | Inputs | Formula | Size* |
|---|---|---|---|
| TAM – Full-service | 281,960 loc [742,000 x 38%, 1] x $2,100 | 281,960 x 2,100 | **$592M** |
| TAM – Institutional | 96,000 kitchens [2] x $2,100 | 96,000 x 2,100 | **$202M** |
| **TAM total** | 377,960 loc x $2,100 | 592+202 | **$794M** |
| **SAM total (Institutional only)** | 96,000 x $2,100 | 96,000 x 2,100 | **$202M** |
| Current – Full-service penetrated | 8,459 loc [281,960 x 3%, 4] x $2,100 | 8,459 x 2,100 | **$18M** |
| Current – Institutional penetrated | 10,560 loc [96,000 x 11%, 4] x $2,100 | 10,560 x 2,100 | **$22M** |
| **Current market total** | 19,019 penetrated loc x $2,100 | 18+22 | **$40M** |

*Rounded to nearest $1M. Context: Wastewise 410 loc x $2,100 ≈ $0.9M ARR, ~2.2% of penetrated units (287 institutional = ~2.7% of penetrated institutional).

## 2. Top-down cross-check

Source [3] "$4.2B food waste tech market" **cannot be used** – it is global and covers hauling/composting/anaerobic digestion, not US tracking software. To reconcile you would need: US share x software-only share, stripping hauling/hardware/services and global locations.

## 3. Competitor snapshot

| Company | Pricing annualized / location (source year) | Hardware model | Latest funding (confidence) | Implication for Wastewise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BinSight (incumbent) | **$1,788/yr** ($149/mo, 2025) | Not disclosed in sources | $22M Series C, 2023 (Medium – company release, dated) | Price anchor ~15% below Wastewise; must win on ROI/retention, not price, esp. in churn-prone independents. |
| Kitchen Ledger | **$2,400/yr + $1,500 one-time kit**; Yr-1 TCO $3,900 (2025) | Separate paid kit | **$14M Series B, Mar 2025** (High – company press release); $40M aggregator claim (Low – contradicted) | Validates institutional willingness to pay premium; upfront kit is friction Wastewise can exploit if hardware bundled. |
| Scrapless | **from $2,148/yr** ($179/mo, 2025); $1,188/yr ($99/mo, 2021 superseded) | Not disclosed in sources | $6M Seed, 2022 (Medium – dated, may not be latest) | +81% entry-price rise signals pricing power/move upmarket; leaves low-end opening but raises bar on unit economics. |
| Wastewise (benchmark) | **$2,100/yr** ACV (data room) | Camera + scale at bin, bundling unclear | n/a | Priced at market midpoint; defensibility hinges on institutional retention vs. Ledger and churn fix vs. BinSight. |

## 4. Source reliability

| Source | Rating | Reason in one line |
|---|---|---|
| [1] National Restaurant Census 2024 | Medium | Broad trade-association count, incentive to inflate and opaque method. |
| [2] Institutional Review 2024 | Medium | Best niche count available but unaudited and hard to verify. |
| [3] Wastewise blog $4.2B | Low | Vendor reuse of global hauling/infrastructure total for software. |
| [4] Greenline penetration 3%/11% | Medium | Timely but sample-based estimates plus qualitative call on limited-service. |
| [5] 2025 pricing pages + Wastewise ACV | High | Primary and current for BinSight/Ledger/Scrapless/Wastewise. |
| [5] TechWire $99/mo 2021 | Low | Stale and superseded by 2025 $179/mo page. |
| [6] Ledger $14M press release | High | Primary company disclosure with lead named. |
| [6] StartupWire $40M aggregator | Low | Secondary and directly contradicted by primary. |
| [6] BinSight $22M / Scrapless $6M releases | Medium | Primary but dated (2023/2022), latest status unconfirmed. |
| [7] Data room 410 loc, 14% churn | Medium | Primary but self-reported, unaudited, churn definition unclear. |

## 5. Open questions for founders (max 5)

1. Unit economics on $2,100 ACV: hardware COGS, install, support/replacement – gross margin and payback?
2. What drives 14% churn in independent full-service – price, labor workflow, or unproven ROI – and why will institutional not follow?
3. Institutional GTM: buyer, sales cycle length, concentration of the ~287 kitchens, and land-and-expand proof?
4. Technical moat vs. BinSight and Kitchen Ledger: measurement accuracy, labor time, POS/inventory integrations?
5. What unlocks full-service and limited-service – franchisor partnership path or low-touch product – or stay institutional-only?
